text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes develop slowly and are often mild, including increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work harder to remove excess glucose, making you pee more often—especially at night—which leads to dehydration and intense thirst.
Constant fatigue: Your cells cannot absorb glucose properly for energy, leaving you feeling exhausted and weak even after resting.
Blurred vision: Fluid shifts in your body can cause the lenses in your eyes to swell and change shape, making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar impairs your immune system and blood flow, causing minor cuts, scrapes, or infections to heal much more slowly.
Tingling or numbness: Nerve damage (neuropathy) can start early, causing a mild tingling, numbness, or burning sensation in your hands or feet.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety, dark patches of skin on your neck, armpits, or groin (called acanthosis nigricans) can signal insulin resistance.
Increased hunger: You might feel very hungry shortly after eating because your body cannot use glucose for fuel effectively.
